 Follow Why SSI recipients will get their November payment early
 Jacquelyn Burrer Thu, October 29, 2026 at 3:28 PM UTC 2 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. More than 575,000 Texans receive Supplemental Security Income payments, according to data from the Social Security Administration. (The Associated Press) An early payday is on the way for some Social Security recipients.
 November's Supplemental Security Income payment is set to arrive this week, meaning some beneficiaries could see two checks this month. Here's what to know.
 Supplemental Security Income is a needs-based program that provides monthly payments to people with limited income and resources who are ages 65 and older, blind or have a qualifying disability.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement More than 575,000 Texans receive SSI payments, according to data from the Social Security Administration.
 The maximum federal SSI payment amounts for 2026 are:
 $994 for an eligible individual
 $1,491 for an eligible individual with an eligible spouse
 $498 for an essential person
 Related : 'Disproportionately impacted': Why a 2027 Social Security COLA may not go as far for people with disabilities 
 SSI benefits are typically paid on the first day of each month. When the first falls on a weekend, payments are issued on the Friday before.
 That means November's payment will be sent out Friday, Oct. 30, rather than Sunday, Nov, 1. A full list of 2026 payment dates can be found on the administration's website, or at ssa.gov/pubs/calendar.htm .
 Advertisement Advertisement If you do not receive your payment on the expected date, the administration recommends waiting three additional mailing days before contacting Social Security.
 Those receiving Social Security benefits will not be impacted and should follow their normal payment schedule .
 Related : Tell us: Are you worried about social security? 
 Will the 2027 Social Security COLA impact SSI payments? 
 Earlier this month, the Social Security Administration announced Social Security recipients will see a 3.6% increase in their monthly benefits next year.
 These benefits include recipients of Social Security, as well as SSI. However, those receiving SSI payments will see payments increase Dec. 31 instead of its usual payment date, as Jan. 1 is a federal holiday.
